Una misma planta dio lugar a costumbres: One plant gave rise to diverse customs. Mate, tereré and chimarrão tell a regional story shaped by Indigenous knowledge, exchange and everyday rituals.
Mucho antes de convertirse en un product: Long before becoming a commercial product, ka'a was part of Guaraní peoples' lives. Its leaves were used in drinks and in social, ritual and medicinal practices within the territory where the plant grows naturally.
Hablar de un único “origen nacional” pro: Speaking of a single “national origin” projects modern borders onto a history that predates them. Yerba culture belongs to a shared region and preserves the depth of the Guaraní legacy through words, techniques and stories.
En guaraní, la palabra se relaciona con: In Guaraní, the word relates both to yerba and to the forest. That connection reminds us that plant, territory and culture are not separate chapters.
Durante el período colonial, el consumo: During the colonial period, consumption spread along the routes of the Río de la Plata basin. The Jesuit missions learned to cultivate the plant, established plantations and expanded its commercial circulation.
Con el tiempo, la yerba atravesó ámbitos: Over time, yerba crossed rural and urban settings and was adopted by very different social groups. Industrialization standardized grinding, packaging and distribution, but did not eliminate local variations: each place kept its objects, gestures and preferences.
Saberes y usos guaraníes en el territori: Guaraní knowledge and practices in the plant's native territory.
Expansión del consumo y desarrollo del c: The spread of consumption and development of cultivation in the missions.
Consolidación de mercados, plantaciones: The consolidation of national markets, plantations and industries.
Una práctica regional que viaja con sus: A regional practice that travels with its communities and keeps changing.
En Argentina el mate atraviesa hogares,: In Argentina, mate is part of homes, work, journeys and gatherings. It can be drunk alone, but a shared round is an immediate way to welcome people and start a conversation.
La producción se concentra en Misiones y: Production is concentrated in Misiones and northeastern Corrientes. Yerba with stems and hot mate predominate in much of the country, although many grinds, vessels and preparation methods coexist. The habit is not a fixed ceremony: it changes across regions, families and generations.
En Uruguay, mate y termo forman una pare: In Uruguay, mate and a thermos form a portable pair. The practice is especially visible in public spaces: it accompanies walks, parks, study, work and conversation.
Es habitual una yerba de molienda fina y: Finely ground yerba with a high leaf content and a strong profile is common. Although the country does not have a large yerba industry of its own, it has developed a material culture and recognizable consumption customs within the region.
El tereré se prepara con agua fría y yer: Tereré is prepared with cold water and yerba mate, and may include pohã ñana: fresh plants crushed and added to the water according to knowledge passed down in families and communities.
La ronda se organiza con una jarra o ter: The round uses a jug or thermos, a guampa and a bombilla. It is an everyday practice of hospitality, dialogue and belonging. In 2020, its traditional practices and knowledge in the culture of pohã ñana were inscribed by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.
El reconocimiento de la UNESCO correspon: UNESCO's recognition covers the complete Paraguayan cultural practice—its knowledge, transmission and customs—not just a cold drink.
En el sur de Brasil, el chimarrão es una: In southern Brazil, chimarrão is one of the most widespread expressions of erva-mate and a symbol of identity and gathering in Rio Grande do Sul.
En 2023, el Instituto do Patrimônio Hist: In 2023, the Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico do Estado registered the “Sistema Cultural e Socioambiental da Erva-Mate Tradicional” as the state's first intangible cultural heritage. The recognition covers traditional cultivation and trade practices linked to different social groups.
El equipo básico parece simple, pero cad: The basic equipment seems simple, but each piece reflects centuries of adaptation. Material, shape and size change the experience and also express local tastes and identities.
Cebar es preparar y servir cada mate. La: Cebar means preparing and serving each mate. The person pouring manages the water, maintains the structure of the yerba and receives the mate back before handing it to the next person.
1 Cargar. Llenar el recipiente con yerb: 1  Fill. Fill the vessel with yerba without packing it completely.
2 Acomodar. Inclinar la yerba para form: 2  Arrange. Tilt the yerba to create a higher side and a lower side.
3 Humedecer. Verter un poco de agua en: 3  Moisten. Pour a little water into the lower side to settle the mixture.
4 Colocar la bombilla. Introducirla en: 4  Place the bombilla. Insert it into the wet area and avoid moving it afterward.
5 Cebar. Servir siempre cerca de la bom: 5  Pour. Always pour near the bombilla to extract the yerba gradually.
No existe una técnica universal. La moli: There is no universal technique. The grind, vessel and local customs change the method; these guidelines are a starting point.
Compartir mate no consiste solo en repar: Sharing mate is more than distributing a drink. The round creates turns, pauses and mutual attention: someone pours, someone receives, drinks and returns it.
Los códigos no son idénticos en toda la: Customs are not identical throughout the region. In many rounds, saying “thank you” means the person does not want any more; the mate returns to the person pouring rather than passing directly from hand to hand. These are agreements learned through observation, not rigid rules or tests of authenticity.
La cultura matera vive porque se transmi: Mate culture lives on because it is passed down and because it changes. Respecting it means recognizing its roots and the diversity of the people who practice it.

Ilex paraguariensis es una especie de la: Ilex paraguariensis is a species in the holly family. It is an evergreen tree native to a subtropical region of South America; its processed leaves and young branches make up yerba mate.
En el monte puede alcanzar varios metros: In the forest it can grow several meters tall. In cultivation it is kept shorter through pruning to care for the plant and make harvesting easier. Yerba mate contains caffeine and theobromine.
“Yerba mate” puede nombrar la planta, el: “Yerba mate” can refer to the plant, the dried product in the bag or the infusion. “Mate” also refers both to the drink and to the vessel it is prepared in.

Su territorio de origen atraviesa fronte: Its original territory crosses present-day borders. The species is native to northeastern Argentina, Paraguay, parts of Brazil and Uruguay, in and around the Paraná Forest and the Atlantic Forest.

El proceso combina cosecha, calor, reduc: The process combines harvesting, heat, size reduction and time. There is no single recipe: aging and the proportions of leaf, stem and dust vary between products.
La molienda no es uniforme. Sus fraccion: The grind is not uniform. Its fractions work together and help explain the flavor, intensity and foam of the infusion.

Elegí un recipiente limpio y una yerba q: Choose a clean vessel and a yerba you want to try. Fill it between 2/3 and 3/4 full: a common guideline, not an absolute rule. Leave room for the water and bombilla.
Tapá la boca con la palma, agitá suaveme: Cover the opening with your palm, shake gently and tilt the vessel again. Aim to leave the yerba higher on one side: this slope is known as the montañita.
Verté un poco de agua tibia en el hueco: Pour a little lukewarm water into the hollow and wait for it to absorb. This initial moistening avoids the sudden temperature change that dry yerba would experience through immediate contact with very hot water.
Introducí la bombilla en el sector húmed: Insert the bombilla into the lower, wet area. Once positioned, avoid moving it unnecessarily: you do not need to stir the yerba between pours.
Usá agua caliente, sin hervir: unos 70–8: Use hot water that has not boiled: around 70–80 °C is a practical guideline for pouring mate. Pour slowly into the same lower area, near the bombilla. Adjust the temperature to your comfort and let it cool if it is too hot to drink.
Conservá parte de la yerba seca arriba y: Keep some dry yerba at the top and gradually work toward it as the flavor weakens. Pouring methods vary by region, grind and person: find one that feels comfortable for you.

Llená con yerba usada, húmeda y recién r: Fill with damp, used yerba freshly removed from a preparation, with no signs of deterioration. If needed, add a little lukewarm water to keep it damp, without overflowing.
